subject: Conjunctions & Adverbial Clauses

sections.instruction: Make sentences with BOTH … AND / EITHER … OR / NEITHER … NOR. (Examples: Tom was late. So was Ann. → Both Tom and Ann were late. He didn't write. He didn't telephone. → He neither wrote nor telephoned.)

questions.prompt: The hotel wasn't clean. And it wasn't comfortable. → Start with: The hotel was
acceptedAnswers: The hotel was neither clean nor comfortable.

questions.prompt: It was a very boring movie. It was very long too. → Start with: The movie was
acceptedAnswers: The movie was both very boring and very long.
The movie was both boring and long.
The movie was both very boring and long.

questions.prompt: Is that man's name Richard? Or is it Robert? It's one of the two. → Start with: That man's name
acceptedAnswers: That man's name is either Richard or Robert.
questions.explanation: either A or B: parallel structure

questions.prompt: I don't have the time to take a vacation. And I don't have the money. → Start with: I have
acceptedAnswers: I have neither the time nor the money to take a vacation.
I have neither time nor money to take a vacation.
I have neither the time nor the money for a vacation.

questions.prompt: We can leave today or we can leave tomorrow - whichever you prefer. → Start with: We
acceptedAnswers: We can leave either today or tomorrow.
We can either leave today or tomorrow.
We can either leave today or leave tomorrow.
questions.explanation: either A or B: parallel structure

questions.prompt: He gave up his job because he needed a change. Also because the pay was low. → Start with: He gave up his job both
acceptedAnswers: He gave up his job both because he needed a change and because the pay was low.

questions.prompt: Laura doesn't smoke. And she doesn't eat meat.
acceptedAnswers: Laura neither smokes nor eats meat.

questions.prompt: The front of the house needs painting. The back needs painting too.
acceptedAnswers: Both the front and the back of the house need painting.
Both the front of the house and the back need painting.
Both the front and back of the house need painting.
questions.explanation: both A and B + plural verb

sections.instruction: Answer the questions. Use paired conjunctions: BOTH … AND. (Example: You have met his father. Have you met his mother? → Yes, I have met both his father and his mother.)

questions.prompt: The driver was injured in the accident. Was the passenger injured in the accident?

sections.instruction: Combine the sentences using the words in brackets: (Example: Jane gave up smoking because she wanted to save money. (in order to) → Jane gave up smoking in order to save money.)

questions.prompt: I came here so that I could see you. (in order to)

questions.prompt: We put up a fence. We want to prevent the rabbit from escaping. (in order to / so that)

We put up a fence to prevent the rabbit from escaping.

questions.prompt: She went shopping so she could buy herself a television. (to)

questions.prompt: I put the food in the fridge because I wanted it to get cold. (in order to)

I put the food in the fridge in order to make it cold.

sections.instruction: Sally and Peter are good friends, but they are very different. Compare Sally and Peter. Join each idea about Sally with the most suitable idea about Peter (list B). Make sentences using WHILE / WHEREAS. (Example: She likes hard work, while / whereas he's quite lazy.)
sections.contextText:
